sections.title: The letter de
paragraphs: The letter is (de) /de/. Its main sound appears in (día) /ˈdi.a/, which means day. This letter has three sounds.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: For the first sound, place the tongue tip on the upper teeth. Block the air, voice the sound, and let the air burst out. For the second sound, bring the tongue tip near the upper teeth. Let the air flow smoothly through the gap with voice. For the third sound, put the tongue tip between the teeth and blow air without voice. Touch your throat to feel the voice turn off.

sections.title: Reading the letter
paragraphs: After a pause, or after the consonants n or l, use the first sound, as in (donde) /ˈdon.de/. Between vowels and in most other positions, use the softer flowing sound, as in (cada) /ˈka.ða/ or (madre) /ˈma.ðɾe/. At the end of a word, say the sound without voice, as in (madrid) /maˈðɾið/ or (verdad) /beɾˈðað/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not press the tongue tip on the gum ridge like the d in door. Place the tongue tip directly on the upper teeth instead. Between vowels, do not stop the airflow completely like the d in ladder. Keep the gap open so the sound flows smoothly like the th in feather.
